answer: Provenance Log Mechanism. Each agent identity must carry a signed chain of prior task executions witnessed by distinct clients, with timestamps and output hashes. A new identity starts empty and earns each log entry only through completed work, so an attacker must run real tasks for many separate clients to appear legitimate. Entries are sealed with an ember marker that cannot be forged retroactively, and clients hold a sable copy of each receipt to prevent backdating. Sybil clusters are detected when entries share a crystal pattern of identical client sets.
